work: Summa de arithmetica, geometria, proportioni et proportionalita
author: Fra Luca Pacioli da Borgo Sansepolcro, O.F.M. (c. 1447 – 1517)

imprint.collation: [8], 224, 76 leaves (in folio, Gothic rotunda type with woodcut mathematical and geometric marginalia)

rights_status: 100% Public Domain (1494 incunable; original GEOMETOR diplomatic transcriptions, English translations, and commentary)

exemplar.institution: Smithsonian Libraries (Dibner Library of the History of Science and Technology, Gift of Bern Dibner / Burndy Library)
exemplar.inspection_method: Direct multimodal page-by-page visual inspection of high-resolution folio scan images (zero OCR reliance)

verified_folios.contents: Title heading & Continentia de tutta lopera
Latin epistle to Marco Sanudo, Pompilius & Sommaripa epigrams, Nov. 20, 1494 register
Italian dedicatory epistle to Duke Guidobaldo da Montefeltro (woodcut initial M)
Continuation of Italian dedication; praise of Federico da Montefeltro & Palazzo Ducale
Conclusion of Italian dedication & Latin dedicatory epistle to Guidobaldo
Incipit of Distinctio I, Tractatus I: La quantita Magnanimo Duca; strapwork border & friar initial L
Quadrivium hierarchy; acknowledgment of Euclid, Boethius, Leonardo Pisano, Jordanus, Blasius of Parma, Sacrobosco, Prosdocimo
Euclid IX.36 generation of even perfect numbers up to Quartus decimus numerus perfectus; Mersenne compositeness warning
Distinctio VI, Tractatus I, Art. 2: Universal necessity of proportion; praise of Piero della Francesca, Alberti, Vitruvius
Arithmetic, geometric, and harmonic progressions & proportionalities
De sex speciebus sive modis arguendi proportionalitatum (conversa, permutata, congionta, disgiunta, eversa, equa)
Boethian proportional arch woodcuts & compounded musical intervals
Distinctio VIII, Tractatus V: Six canonical Cossic equations & Latin mnemonic verses (Primi/Secundi/Tertii canonis versus)
Euclidean Book II gnomon demonstrations of compound quadratic canons with marginal square-completion woodcuts
Higher Cossic power gradations (cosa, censo, cubo, censo de censo) & reducible biquadratics
Historic verdict that general cubics lack a general algebraic rule, compared to squaring the circle
Distinctio IX, Tractatus X: Giuoco della balla & Problem 51 three-player balestrare (4, 3, 2) to 6 for 10 ducats
Incipit of Tractatus XI: Particularis de computis et scripturis (Cap. 1–2: cash, credit, Inventario)
Cap. 6–9: Memoriale, authentication of books at the Consoli de mercanti, nine modes of purchasing
Cap. 10–12: Giornale structure, Per // A terminology, Cassa non-negativity invariant
Cap. 12–13: Opening Giornale entry (8 Nov 1493), Quaderno cross-indexing, Venetian l. s. g. p. currency standard
Cap. 14: Fundamental conservation law of double-entry posting & diagonal cancelling lines
Summary epilogue (Tariffa / Ricordanze) closing De computis et scripturis
Tractatus Geometriae, Dist. I, Cap. 1: Point, line, surface, Euclid Book I–II digest
Euclid Book I propositions & marginal geometric diagrams
Dist. I, Cap. 8: Heron's formula & cathetus derivation on the (13, 14, 15) triangle (area = sqrt(7056) = 84)
Dist. III, Cap. 6: Archimedes's 96-gon circle measurement (3 10/71 < pi < 3 1/7)
Dist. VI: Three equal circles inscribed in the (10, 10, 12) triangle (5 3/4 censi + 16 cose = 48)
Dist. VIII: De corporibus regularibus — Tetrahedron and Cube in sphere D = 6
Dist. VIII, prob. 15–17: Truncated tetrahedron (edge sqrt(6 6/11)) & cuboctahedron (edge 3) in sphere D = 6
Dist. VIII, prob. 18–22: Cuboctahedron volume, Archimedes hydrostatics, dodecahedron edge sqrt(20) - 2 in sphere axis sqrt(48)
Paganino de' Paganini Venice colophon (10 Nov. 1494) under Doge Agostino Barbarigo & 10-year privilege
